claims.text: Refining the microstructure increases grain-boundary density.
High grain-boundary density accelerates migration of reactive elements such as Cr, Al, Si, or Ti to the alloy surface.
Accelerated reactive-element transport produces a continuous, self-healing protective oxide scale.
Localized protective-oxide formation at grain boundaries limits oxide spallation and crack propagation.
A refined microstructure improves oxidation resistance relative to a coarse-grained microstructure.
The initial material is a relatively coarse-grained BCC/FCC or related solid-solution multiprincipal-element alloy.
The initial material has an inhomogeneous elemental distribution.
Stationary friction processing can refine an approximately 98 micrometer as-cast grain size to approximately 1 or 0.43 micrometers.
Severe plastic deformation or rapid-solidification methods such as selective laser melting will provide the same grain-refinement intervention.
The proposed behavior is relevant during sustained oxidation at approximately 850–1100 degrees Celsius.
The protective oxide phases may include Cr2O3, Al2O3, or SiO2.
Grain boundaries act as fast diffusion pathways for reactive alloying elements.
Reactive alloying elements preferentially oxidize at the surface to form a continuous and adherent scale.
A continuous protective scale slows further oxidation and resists thermally induced cracking and spallation.
Refined AlCoCrFeNi exhibits lower oxidation kinetics and lower cumulative mass gain than its as-cast counterpart.
Refined samples will exhibit fewer oxide-scale cracks and spallation events than coarse-grained samples.
Refined samples will retain better overall material integrity after prolonged oxidation.
The hypothesis may fail when alloy chemistry or environmental conditions favor nonprotective oxides.
Processing-induced porosity may dominate oxidation behavior and negate the proposed grain-boundary effect.
A valid comparison uses identical alloy chemistry and oxidation conditions while varying processing to produce coarse and refined microstructures.
